intro: A small bowl of kuah dal is about 150 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the lentils and the oil or ghee used for tempering.

variants.name: Kuah dal banjir over rice (3 ladles)
Dal with extra ghee (1 small bowl)

diet: Absolutely. Dal has protein and fibre that help you stay full longer. It's a lighter choice than the santan curry gravy at nasi kandar shops. Just keep an eye on the ghee and how much rice you eat with it.
tips: At nasi kandar, ask for kuah dal instead of oily mixed curry gravy.
Pair dal with ayam tandoori or a boiled egg for more protein.
Cooking at home? Temper with just 1 teaspoon of oil. The spices already give enough flavour.

swap.name: Homemade vegetable dal without ghee
swap.why: More vegetables, less oil, but the spice flavour is still there.

faq.q: What lentils is dal made from?
faq.a: Usually yellow lentils (toor dal) or red lentils (masoor). Some also mix in chana dal.

faq.q: Is dal enough as a protein source?
faq.a: Dal has protein, but a small bowl only gives about 7 g. Better to add chicken, fish, egg or tofu to your meal.

faq.q: Why does dal sometimes make me bloated?
faq.a: Beans and lentils can cause gas. Wash and soak the dal before cooking, and cook until really soft.
